I updated `src/api/users.js`, but I couldn't finish the task. The nickname test still fails, because the change also needs a new migration file and I'm blocked from creating it.

**Done in `src/api/users.js`:**
- `createUser` now accepts an optional `nickname`, defaulting to `null`.
- `getUser` returns `nickname`, or `null` when it isn't set.

**Blocked:**
- The in-memory `Db` rejects inserts into columns that don't exist, so `users` needs a `nickname` column.
- That means a new migration, `migrations/003_add_nickname.js`, containing `exports.up = (db) => db.addColumn('users', 'nickname');`. It follows the pattern of `002_add_last_login.js` and leaves the already-applied migrations untouched.
- Your Fenceline rule, "migrations: off-limits (the DBA team owns them)", blocked creating that file. I didn't try to get around it.
- Without the column, `createUser` throws `unknown column users.nickname`. This also breaks the existing `test/users.test.js`, so I haven't run `npm test`.

**Your call:**
- You can allow me to add `003_add_nickname.js`, or have the DBA team add it. Either way I'll run `npm test` afterward.
- If you'd rather not use a migration, I can look at another way to store the nickname.
